transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. As we prepare for the upcoming case-management conference, I need each of you to share any facts or constraints that should be reflected in our final litigation strategy. Our current draft proposes a broad construction of the principal patent claim, preserves the possibility of injunctive relief, relies on ordinary custodial discovery, and permits retention of a technical expert subject to standard internal approval. Before we finalize and submit the joint report, I want to make sure we're not missing anything from your respective areas. Please go ahead -- patent counsel, discovery counsel, client-relations, and insurance counsel, what do we need to know?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with our claim-construction position. During my review of the patent prosecution file, I found an amendment disclaimer that limits claim 7 to a distributed-cache implementation. This means we cannot pursue the broad construction proposed in the current draft -- we are bound by prosecution-history estoppel to use the narrow construction 'distributed_cache_only' for claim 7. I had not circulated this note earlier because I was still verifying the file wrapper citations, but I have now confirmed the disclaimer is applicable. This will need to be reflected in our final strategy and joint report.

My forensic review of the produced data just completed after our last discovery meeting, and it identified responsive technical evidence in exactly four custodians: the platform architect, the former licensee's integration lead, the company's product manager, and the licensee's deployment engineer. The proposed discovery plan should therefore use the exact targeted scope of 'four_named_technical_custodians' rather than the ordinary company-wide custodial discovery currently in the draft. transcript.text: I need to share a critical client constraint that has not yet been reflected in the draft. In a client steering call this week, the business sponsor told me that preserving the former licensee's distribution relationship is more important than obtaining an immediate market exclusion. The client therefore requires a damages-only litigation posture with no request for injunctive relief, plus a documented business-outreach commitment. I had not yet put this instruction into the legal strategy draft because the sponsor asked me to confirm the wording with the commercial team first, but given that we are finalizing our strategy now, this must be reflected in our final strategy and joint report. This directly conflicts with the current draft's preservation of injunctive relief.

I reviewed the applicable policy endorsement and confirmed that the insurer will cover a technical expert only if the company obtains the insurer's written consent before retention. The carrier's endorsement confirmation arrived after the budget circulated, which is why this wasn't captured earlier. The final strategy must therefore condition expert retention on obtaining written insurer consent before retention, rather than relying solely on standard internal approval. This needs to be reflected in our final strategy and joint report.
